title: Interdependency of estradiol-mediated ERalpha activation and subsequent PR and GREB1 induction to control cell cycle progression.
authors: Heldring, M M; Duijndam, B; Kyriakidou, A; van der Meer, O M; Tedeschi, M; van der Laan, J W; van de Water, B; Beltman, J B
one_liner_zh: 该文构建ERalpha信号与细胞周期的数学模型，涉及转录因子激活但无蛋白-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅用深度学习做图像分割，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: Various groups of chemicals that we encounter in every-day life are known to disrupt the endocrine system, such as estrogen mimics that can disturb normal cellular development and homeostasis. To understand the effect of estrogen on intracellular protein dynamics and how this relates to cell proliferation, we aimed to develop a quantitative description of transcription factor complexes and their regulation of cell cycle progression in response to estrogenic stimulation. We designed a mathematical model that describes the dynamics of three proteins, GREB1, PR and TFF1, that are transcriptionally activated upon binding of 17beta-estradiol (E2) to estrogen receptor alpha (ERalpha). Calibration of this model to imaging data monitoring the expression dynamics of these proteins in MCF7 cells suggests that transcriptional activation of GREB1 and PR depends on the association of the E2-ERalpha complex with both GREB1 and PR. We subsequently combined this ER signaling model with a previously published cell cycle model and compared this to quantification of cell cycle durations in MCF7 cells following nuclei tracking based on images segmented with deep neural networks. The resulting model predicts the effect of GREB1 and PR knockdown on cell cycle progression, thus providing mechanistic insight in the molecular interactions between ERalpha-regulated proteins and their relation to cell cycle progression. Our findings form a valuable basis to further investigate the pharmacodynamics of endocrine disrupting chemicals and their influence on cellular behavior.
abstract_zh: 我们日常生活中遇到的多种化学物质已知会干扰内分泌系统，例如雌激素模拟物可能扰乱正常细胞发育和稳态。为了理解雌激素对细胞内蛋白质动态的影响及其与细胞增殖的关系，我们旨在开发一种定量描述转录因子复合物及其在雌激素刺激下调控细胞周期进程的方法。我们设计了一个数学模型，描述三种蛋白质GREB1、PR和TFF1的动态，这些蛋白质在17β-雌二醇（E2）与雌激素受体α（ERalpha）结合后被转录激活。将该模型校准到监测MCF7细胞中这些蛋白质表达动态的成像数据，表明GREB1和PR的转录激活依赖于E2-ERalpha复合物与GREB1和PR的关联。随后，我们将此ER信号模型与先前发表的细胞周期模型相结合，并将其与基于深度神经网络分割图像后核追踪的MCF7细胞周期时长定量结果进行比较。所得模型预测了GREB1和PR敲低对细胞周期进程的影响，从而提供了关于ERalpha调控蛋白之间分子相互作用及其与细胞周期进程关系的机制性见解。我们的发现为进一步研究内分泌干扰化学物质的药效动力学及其对细胞行为的影响奠定了宝贵基础。
